findings.evidence: First answer three questions. Who will see it: team Slack, a PR, or a public post? Who is the butt of the joke ... Which channel, and does its tone allow it?
findings.fix: Replace the three audience questions, which restate social sense the model already has, with one line: "Aim the joke at the situation or tool, never a named person, and match the channel's tone." Keep the payoff-first rule and the character limits.

findings.evidence: Captions travel in the URL to a public third-party service, which logs them ... Replace customer names, tokens or credentials, internal URLs or hostnames
findings.fix: Add a Gotcha: "Never pass an internal or signed image URL to --background or --style. memegen.link fetches it from the public internet, so a private URL either fails or leaks a signed link into the meme URL and the service's logs. Ask for a public image URL instead."

findings.evidence: "Uses a failure-appropriate template such as `fine` and concise text." (precise-meme has the same wording: "Uses concise captions"), and text-only-greentext lists the skill's own references/markdown-memes-guide.md under files instead of an input file
findings.fix: Make the assertions countable, for example "each caption is 30 characters or fewer before escaping" and "template id is one of fine, buzz". Remove the skill's own reference from `files`, or replace it with a real input under evals/files/.

Add a note: "Single quotes break when a caption has an apostrophe (I don't always, it's fine). Use double quotes for those captions, or write ' as '\''. The helper keeps ' raw in the URL." Also mention that --alt text with ] or ) breaks the Markdown image, because the helper does not escape it.
